name: Polygon
technique: Missing balance check in MRC20 transfer-with-signature
rootCause: The native MATIC (MRC20) system contract failed to validate the signer and balance in transferWithSig, putting ~9.2B MATIC at risk. Whitehats reported it; an attacker stole ~801,601 MATIC before a hard fork patched it.

On December 3, a group of white hat hackers notified Polygon’s vulnerability bounty agency Immunefi of a vulnerability in the Polygon PoS creation contract. The Polygon core team contacted the organization and Immunefi's expert team and immediately launched a repair procedure. Validators and the full-node community are notified to upgrade 80% of the network without interruption within 24 hours. The upgrade was performed on December 5th at block #22156660, which did not affect the activity and performance of the network. The vulnerability has been fixed and the damage has been mitigated, with no substantial damage to the agreement and its end users. All…

Polygon suffered a critical access control failure in December 2021. An attacker exploited a missing authorization check, stealing about 801,601 MATIC (~$2.04M) before a hard fork secured remaining funds. Detailed technical evidence and exploit transactions remain undisclosed. The affected Polygon Proof-of-Stake Genesis contract contained an improper access control vulnerability, specifically a missing authorization or balance check. This flaw allowed unauthorized transfers and exposed the protocol to significant risk before emergency patching.
